## Mixed Distribution Likelihood (Unknown Spine)

When the spine individual is unknown, each observed age could be either

- a non-spine draw with density $f(x_i; \lambda, \mu)$, or
- the unique spine draw with density $g(x_i; \lambda, \mu)$.

If there are $n$ observed ages and exactly one is the spine (uniformly over
positions), the age-component likelihood is

$$
  L_{\text{ages}}(\lambda, \mu)
  = \frac{1}{n}\sum_{k=1}^n
  \left[
  g(x_k; \lambda, \mu)
  \prod_{i\neq k} f(x_i; \lambda, \mu)
  \right].
$$

Equivalent log form:

$$
  \ell_{\text{ages}}(\lambda, \mu)
  = \sum_{i=1}^n \log f(x_i; \lambda, \mu)
  - \log n
  + \log\!\left(\sum_{k=1}^n
  \exp\!\big(\log g(x_k; \lambda, \mu)-\log f(x_k; \lambda, \mu)\big)
  \right).
$$

For numerical stability, define

$$
  a_k = \log g(x_k; \lambda, \mu)-\log f(x_k; \lambda, \mu),
$$

and compute the inner term with log-sum-exp:

$$
  \log\sum_{k=1}^n e^{a_k} = \operatorname{logsumexp}(a_1,\dots,a_n).
$$

The full objective adds the population term:

$$
  \ell(\lambda, \mu)
  = \log P_n(T\mid \lambda,\mu)
  + \ell_{\text{ages}}(\lambda,\mu).
$$

```{python}
def _major_gridline_values(domain_max: float, target_count: int = 5) -> list[float]:
    """Round-number gridline positions spanning ``[0, domain_max]``.

    Vega-Lite draws one gridline per bin edge on a binned quantitative axis
    by default (``tickCount``/``nice`` on the scale don't override this for
    binned fields), which is far denser than useful here. Explicit
    round-number ``axis.values`` (step chosen from ``{1, 2, 2.5, 5} x 10^k``,
    the standard "nice number" ladder) is the only way to get sparse,
    human-readable gridlines on a binned axis.
    """
    if domain_max <= 0:
        return [0.0]
    raw_step = domain_max / target_count
    magnitude = 10 ** np.floor(np.log10(raw_step))
    step = magnitude
    for mult in (1, 2, 2.5, 5, 10):
        step = mult * magnitude
        if step >= raw_step:
            break
    return [
        float(v) for v in np.arange(0.0, domain_max + step, step) if v <= domain_max
    ]

def print_rate_summary(label: str, birth_values: Any, death_values: Any) -> None:
    birth_array = np.asarray(birth_values, dtype=np.float64)
    death_array = np.asarray(death_values, dtype=np.float64)

    if birth_array.size == 0 or death_array.size == 0:
        print(f"{label}: no successful fits to summarize.")
        return

    parameter_matrix = np.column_stack([birth_array, death_array])
    means = np.mean(parameter_matrix, axis=0)
    medians = np.median(parameter_matrix, axis=0)
    covariance_matrix = np.cov(parameter_matrix, rowvar=False)

    print(f"\n{label}")
    print(f"- Mean birth rate: {means[0]:.6f}")
    print(f"- Median birth rate: {medians[0]:.6f}")
    print(f"- Mean death rate: {means[1]:.6f}")
    print(f"- Median death rate: {medians[1]:.6f}")
    print("- Covariance matrix:")
    print(covariance_matrix)


all_birth_values = fit_birth_values + fit_birth_values_boundary
all_death_values = fit_death_values + fit_death_values_boundary
print_rate_summary(
    "Summary statistics for all successful fits", all_birth_values, all_death_values
)
```

## Joint Heatmaps of Fitted Rates

```{python}
def _one_sided_upper_iqr_mask(
    values: np.ndarray, whisker_width: float = 1.5
) -> np.ndarray:
    """Keep values below the upper IQR fence; never drop the lower tail.

    μ fits legitimately cluster near 0, so the symmetric two-sided IQR filter
    used for λ would wrongly cut off small-but-valid fits. Only values far
    ABOVE the third quartile are treated as outliers here.
    """
    finite = np.isfinite(values)
    if not finite.any():
        return finite
    q1, q3 = np.percentile(values[finite], [25.0, 75.0])
    iqr = q3 - q1
    if not np.isfinite(iqr) or iqr == 0.0:
        return finite
    upper_bound = q3 + whisker_width * iqr
    return finite & (values <= upper_bound)


def _heatmap_subset(
    births: np.ndarray, deaths: np.ndarray
) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
    """Joint λ/μ plotting subset: two-sided IQR for λ, upper-only for μ."""
    _, lambda_mask = iqr_plotting_subset({"lambda": births})
    mu_mask = _one_sided_upper_iqr_mask(deaths)
    mask = lambda_mask & mu_mask
    return births[mask], deaths[mask]


def _fitted_heatmap(
    births: np.ndarray,
    deaths: np.ndarray,
    title: str,
    save_name: str,
    output_dir: "Path | None" = None,
) -> None:
    """Display and save a binned λ-vs-μ count heatmap with the true value marked."""
    if births.size == 0 or deaths.size == 0:
        print(f"No data for {title}")
        return
    df = pd.DataFrame({"lambda": births, "mu": deaths})
    lambda_min = min(float(births.min()), birth_rate)
    lambda_max = max(float(births.max()), birth_rate)
    mu_max = max(float(deaths.max()), death_rate)
    cells = (
        alt.Chart(df)
        .mark_rect()
        .encode(
            # x starts at the filtered minimum (not 0) since λ never clusters
            # near zero the way μ does; y stays anchored at 0 for μ.
            x=alt.X(
                "lambda:Q",
                bin=alt.Bin(maxbins=25),
                title="Fitted λ",
                scale=alt.Scale(domain=[lambda_min, lambda_max]),
            ),
            y=alt.Y(
                "mu:Q",
                bin=alt.Bin(maxbins=25),
                title="Fitted μ",
                scale=alt.Scale(domain=[0, mu_max]),
            ),
            color=alt.Color("count():Q", title="Count"),
        )
    )

    # Two perpendicular dotted lines mark the true λ/μ (clearer than a single
    # cross marker at their intersection, and each line reads unambiguously
    # against either axis). Both share one "true value" legend entry.
    _truth_scale = alt.Scale(domain=["true value"], range=["black"])
    _truth_legend = alt.Legend(title=None, orient="top")
    truth_v = (
        alt.Chart(pd.DataFrame({"lambda": [birth_rate], "kind": ["true value"]}))
        .mark_rule(strokeDash=[4, 2])
        .encode(
            x="lambda:Q",
            color=alt.Color("kind:N", scale=_truth_scale, legend=_truth_legend),
        )
    )
    truth_h = (
        alt.Chart(pd.DataFrame({"mu": [death_rate], "kind": ["true value"]}))
        .mark_rule(strokeDash=[4, 2])
        .encode(
            y="mu:Q",
            color=alt.Color("kind:N", scale=_truth_scale, legend=_truth_legend),
        )
    )
    fig = (cells + truth_v + truth_h).properties(title=title, width=400, height=350)
    display(fig)
    save_chart(fig, save_name, width=300, height=200, output_dir=output_dir)
    print(f"Saved {save_name}")


# λ uses the standard two-sided IQR filter; μ only drops fits far above the
# upper fence, so near-zero (but valid) μ fits are never excluded.
_heat_all_lambda, _heat_all_mu = _heatmap_subset(
    np.asarray(fit_birth_values + fit_birth_values_boundary, dtype=np.float64),
    np.asarray(fit_death_values + fit_death_values_boundary, dtype=np.float64),
)
_heat_nb_lambda, _heat_nb_mu = _heatmap_subset(
    np.asarray(fit_birth_values, dtype=np.float64),
    np.asarray(fit_death_values, dtype=np.float64),
)

_heatmap_datasets = [
    (
        _heat_all_lambda,
        _heat_all_mu,
        "Fitted λ vs μ — All fits, IQR subset",
        "vse06_rate_heatmap_all",
    ),
    (
        _heat_nb_lambda,
        _heat_nb_mu,
        "Fitted λ vs μ — Excluding boundary fits, IQR subset",
        "vse06_rate_heatmap_non_boundary",
    ),
]
for _lambda_vals, _mu_vals, _heat_title, _heat_save_name in _heatmap_datasets:
    _fitted_heatmap(
        births=_lambda_vals,
        deaths=_mu_vals,
        title=_heat_title,
        save_name=_heat_save_name,
        output_dir=figures_dir,
    )
```

## Fitted Rates vs Population Size

```{python}
_rate_color = alt.Scale(
    domain=["lambda", "mu", "lambda-mu"], range=[PTOLQUAL[0], PTOLQUAL[1], PTOLQUAL[2]]
)
_shape_scale = alt.Scale(domain=["non-boundary", "boundary"], range=["circle", "cross"])

if len(fit_populations) > 0 or len(fit_populations_boundary) > 0:
    # IQR-filter each group independently to reduce point density for interactive display.
    _nb_pop_filt, _ = iqr_plotting_subset(
        {
            "x": np.asarray(fit_populations, dtype=np.float64),
            "lambda": np.asarray(fit_birth_values, dtype=np.float64),
            "mu": np.asarray(fit_death_values, dtype=np.float64),
            "growth": np.asarray(fit_growth_values, dtype=np.float64),
        }
    )
    _b_pop_filt, _ = iqr_plotting_subset(
        {
            "x": np.asarray(fit_populations_boundary, dtype=np.float64),
            "lambda": np.asarray(fit_birth_values_boundary, dtype=np.float64),
            "mu": np.asarray(fit_death_values_boundary, dtype=np.float64),
            "growth": np.asarray(fit_growth_values_boundary, dtype=np.float64),
        }
    )
    _pop_rows: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    for x, lam, mu, gro in zip(
        _nb_pop_filt["x"].tolist(),
        _nb_pop_filt["lambda"].tolist(),
        _nb_pop_filt["mu"].tolist(),
        _nb_pop_filt["growth"].tolist(),
    ):
        _pop_rows += [
            {"x": x, "y": lam, "rate": "lambda", "boundary": "non-boundary"},
            {"x": x, "y": mu, "rate": "mu", "boundary": "non-boundary"},
            {"x": x, "y": gro, "rate": "lambda-mu", "boundary": "non-boundary"},
        ]
    for x, lam, mu, gro in zip(
        _b_pop_filt["x"].tolist(),
        _b_pop_filt["lambda"].tolist(),
        _b_pop_filt["mu"].tolist(),
        _b_pop_filt["growth"].tolist(),
    ):
        _pop_rows += [
            {"x": x, "y": lam, "rate": "lambda", "boundary": "boundary"},
            {"x": x, "y": mu, "rate": "mu", "boundary": "boundary"},
            {"x": x, "y": gro, "rate": "lambda-mu", "boundary": "boundary"},
        ]
    _pop_df = pd.DataFrame(_pop_rows)
    # Click a group in the legend to toggle boundary/non-boundary points (HTML only).
    _pop_bnd_select = alt.selection_point(fields=["boundary"], bind="legend")
    _pop_pts = (
        alt.Chart(_pop_df)
        .mark_point(opacity=0.25, filled=True)
        .encode(
            x=alt.X("x:Q", title="Population size", scale=alt.Scale(zero=True)),
            y=alt.Y("y:Q", title="Fitted rate", scale=alt.Scale(zero=True)),
            color=alt.Color(
                "rate:N", scale=_rate_color, legend=alt.Legend(title=None, orient="top")
            ),
            shape=alt.Shape(
                "boundary:N",
                scale=_shape_scale,
                legend=alt.Legend(title=None, orient="top"),
            ),
            size=alt.condition(
                alt.datum["boundary"] == "boundary", alt.value(60), alt.value(25)
            ),
        )
        .transform_filter(_pop_bnd_select)
        .add_params(_pop_bnd_select)
    )
    _birth_rule = (
        alt.Chart(pd.DataFrame({"y": [birth_rate]}))
        .mark_rule(strokeDash=[4, 2], color=PTOLQUAL[0], opacity=0.8)
        .encode(y="y:Q")
    )
    _death_rule = (
        alt.Chart(pd.DataFrame({"y": [death_rate]}))
        .mark_rule(strokeDash=[4, 2], color=PTOLQUAL[1], opacity=0.8)
        .encode(y="y:Q")
    )
    fig_rates_vs_pop = (_pop_pts + _birth_rule + _death_rule).properties(
        title="Fitted Rates vs Population Size", width=500, height=350
    )
    display(fig_rates_vs_pop)
    save_chart(
        fig_rates_vs_pop,
        "vse06_rates_vs_population_size",
        width=300,
        height=200,
        output_dir=figures_dir,
    )
    print("Saved rates-vs-population figure")
```

```{python}
if len(fit_mean_ages) > 0 or len(fit_mean_ages_boundary) > 0:
    # IQR-filter each group independently to reduce point density for interactive display.
    _nb_age_filt, _ = iqr_plotting_subset(
        {
            "x": np.asarray(fit_mean_ages, dtype=np.float64),
            "lambda": np.asarray(fit_birth_values, dtype=np.float64),
            "mu": np.asarray(fit_death_values, dtype=np.float64),
        }
    )
    _b_age_filt, _ = iqr_plotting_subset(
        {
            "x": np.asarray(fit_mean_ages_boundary, dtype=np.float64),
            "lambda": np.asarray(fit_birth_values_boundary, dtype=np.float64),
            "mu": np.asarray(fit_death_values_boundary, dtype=np.float64),
        }
    )
    _age_rows: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    for x, lam, mu in zip(
        _nb_age_filt["x"].tolist(),
        _nb_age_filt["lambda"].tolist(),
        _nb_age_filt["mu"].tolist(),
    ):
        _age_rows += [
            {"x": x, "y": lam, "rate": "lambda", "boundary": "non-boundary"},
            {"x": x, "y": mu, "rate": "mu", "boundary": "non-boundary"},
        ]
    for x, lam, mu in zip(
        _b_age_filt["x"].tolist(),
        _b_age_filt["lambda"].tolist(),
        _b_age_filt["mu"].tolist(),
    ):
        _age_rows += [
            {"x": x, "y": lam, "rate": "lambda", "boundary": "boundary"},
            {"x": x, "y": mu, "rate": "mu", "boundary": "boundary"},
        ]
    _age_df = pd.DataFrame(_age_rows)
    # Click a group in the legend to toggle boundary/non-boundary points (HTML only).
    _age_bnd_select = alt.selection_point(fields=["boundary"], bind="legend")
    _age_pts = (
        alt.Chart(_age_df)
        .mark_point(opacity=0.25, filled=True)
        .encode(
            x=alt.X("x:Q", title="Mean population age", scale=alt.Scale(zero=True)),
            y=alt.Y("y:Q", title="Fitted rate", scale=alt.Scale(zero=True)),
            color=alt.Color(
                "rate:N", scale=_rate_color, legend=alt.Legend(title=None, orient="top")
            ),
            shape=alt.Shape(
                "boundary:N",
                scale=_shape_scale,
                legend=alt.Legend(title=None, orient="top"),
            ),
            size=alt.condition(
                alt.datum["boundary"] == "boundary", alt.value(60), alt.value(25)
            ),
        )
        .transform_filter(_age_bnd_select)
        .add_params(_age_bnd_select)
    )
    _birth_rule2 = (
        alt.Chart(pd.DataFrame({"y": [birth_rate]}))
        .mark_rule(strokeDash=[4, 2], color=PTOLQUAL[0], opacity=0.8)
        .encode(y="y:Q")
    )
    _death_rule2 = (
        alt.Chart(pd.DataFrame({"y": [death_rate]}))
        .mark_rule(strokeDash=[4, 2], color=PTOLQUAL[1], opacity=0.8)
        .encode(y="y:Q")
    )
    fig_rates_vs_mean_age = (_age_pts + _birth_rule2 + _death_rule2).properties(
        title="Fitted Rates vs Mean Population Age", width=500, height=350
    )
    display(fig_rates_vs_mean_age)
    save_chart(
        fig_rates_vs_mean_age,
        "vse06_rates_vs_mean_population_age",
        width=300,
        height=200,
        output_dir=figures_dir,
    )
    print("Saved rates-vs-mean-age figure")
```

```{python}
import json
import os
import time
from pathlib import Path

doc_name = "methods_validation_bulk_inference.qmd"

compile_log = project_dir / "_output" / "compile_times.json"

duration_seconds = time.perf_counter() - __compile_start

try:
    data = json.loads(compile_log.read_text()) if compile_log.exists() else {}
except Exception:
    data = {}

data[doc_name] = {"duration_seconds": duration_seconds, "timestamp": timestamp}
```
